plain: To repay someone for a loss or protect them against one.

webster.text: To save harmless; to secure against loss, damage or penalty.

example.quote: It is not to be presumed that he will not add to the price a sum sufficient to indemnify himself for the inconvenience of parting with the money he pays as a duty.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 4, North Carolina Convention, Gov. JOHNSTON, July 26, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
